references.saccade_duration: Carpenter (1988), Movements of the Eyes: D ~ 21 ms + 2.2 ms/deg (approx., 5-50 deg)
references.saccade_peak_velocity: Bahill, Clark & Stark (1975) main sequence; peak velocity rises with amplitude and saturates around 400-600 deg/s; ~300-450 deg/s for 10-20 deg saccades is typical of reported means
references.pursuit: Lisberger, Morris & Tychsen (1987): pursuit latency ~100-150 ms; steady-state gain ~0.9-1.0 for slow (<~0.5 Hz) targets
references.vergence: geometry: each eye aims at the same 3-D point; vergence angle = 2*atan((IPD/2)/d) for a midline target
references.blink: Blink duration typically ~100-400 ms with the closing phase faster than the opening phase (e.g. VanderWerf et al. 2003)
references.fixation: Drift during fixation is a slow random walk of the order of minutes of arc (e.g. Rolfs 2009 review); microsaccades are not modelled

saccade.note: peak velocity = 1.875*A/D for a minimum-jerk profile; compare with the reference range, not a fitted human dataset

blink.note: closure curve only; lid bones are not driven to full closure (see KNOWN_LIMITATIONS)
